channel.title: Scottish Left Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Scottish Left Review (scottishleftreview.scot)

item.title: Commons Sense
item.description: Kat Hunfeld reflects on a doom-defying gathering of land activists and the small steps being taken towards collective land ownership in Scotland.

item.title: Political Economy and the Future of Land Reform
item.description: The 2025 Land Reform Act is not the land settlement Scotland needs, but a platform on which further reform can be built, writes Ariane Burgess MSP.

item.title: Land, Power, and the Future We Choose
item.description: Just transition is at a crossroads, but its next stage could lead to a fairer land settlement for Scotland, writes Satwat Rehman.

item.title: The Transition to Defence Dependency
item.description: As Scotland exits oil and gas, Craig Stockwell investigates its tightening ties to Transatlantic defence procurement and the military-industrial complex.

item.title: The Aberdeen Problem
item.description: Hailed for decades as the Oil and Gas Capital of Europe, the city of Aberdeen faces an existential crisis. Iona MacDonald asks why so little is being done to prevent it.

item.title: Farmers Against Fascism
item.description: The Left's lack of interest in rural workers is helping drive more people into the arms of the far right, but now land workers are organising, write Suhail Merchant and Tara Wight.

item.title: A New Generation of Community Wind-Wealth
item.description: The Danish model demonstrates how Scotland's communities could co-own wind farms, writes Calum MacDonald.

item.title: Editorial: The Land Struggle Continues
item.description: Cailean Gallagher introduces this issue, which illustrates the value of the whole Left becoming involved in the land struggle.

item.title: Buying Time for Other People
item.description: Everybody to Kenmure Street, the new film by Felipe Bustos Sierra, portrays the power of laying our bodies on the line, writes Christopher Silver.
